text: {"lessons":["My Stock D sale at a steep loss shows that avoiding the pain of realizing losses can let a position deteriorate; reassess each holding using its current prospects and risk, not its cost basis.","Selling Stock A after a large gain felt rewarding, but repeated profit-taking can leave too little invested in a strong performer; let expected future return and portfolio balance guide the size of any sale.","Buying more of Stocks B and E after trimming them, while also making mixed results across the account, reminds me to evaluate each trade as part of a consistent portfolio plan rather than reacting to recent prices or the urge to lock in gains."]}
